transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Video call
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE); Miles Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Atlas Retail - Head of ML Ops); Damien Ko (Atlas - VP Eng); Lena Ortiz (Atlas - Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Renew/expand, customer wants APAC and EU private. Discussed lead times, pricing, compliance.

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we got Priya, Damien, Lena from Atlas, and Miles and I from Redwood. how's everyone doing?
00:07 Priya (Atlas): Good, thanks. hey Sofia. busy prep for Q4, so trying to lock these pieces down.
00:12 Damien (Atlas): Afternoon. want to be efficient — timeline is tight.
:18 Sofia: Great. goal for today is to confirm the uplift numbers, timelines for APAC/onprem eu, and agree next steps on contract. Miles will walk through technical lead times.
01:05 Miles (Redwood SE): Cool. quick context: we reviewed Atlas's usage patterns. looking at a ~40% reserved capacity increase to cover peak shopping windows, plus a smaller APAC burst pool. for EU you mentioned wanting private deployment — VPC with customer-managed control plane, right?
01:20 Priya: Correct. EU must keep PII in-region and we need auditability. also want to avoid cross-border caching for failed fallbacks.
01:34 Lena (Security): And from compliance we'll need SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and role-based access logging. can you share the audit logs retention options?
01:45 Miles: Yes — we have per-request audit logs and can retain at the route/model level. default retention is 90 days in hosted, but for private we can configure long term retention. I will send the retention options doc.
02:12 Damien: On the dedicated capacity — what's the provisioning lead time if we add +40%? we can't afford more than a three-week delay.
02:20 Miles: Typical provisioning for reserved GPU pools is 10–21 business days depending on queue and region. APAC often takes a bit longer due to capacity constraints, so plan on three weeks for apac-south unless we do a prioritized provisioning (which adds cost).
03:05 Priya: What about latency SLOs? our UX team wants p95 < 220ms for short responses. are those realistic from apac and eu private?
03:15 Miles: For shorter sequences, yes — with dedicated capacity and our KV cache you should see p95 in the 150–250ms range. EU private depends on on-prem network, but if it's co-located in eu-west edge region we hit similar numbers. we'll need to run benchmark traffic to confirm.
04:00 Damien: Pricing — we were expecting a better committed rate if we lock a 12-month term. can you outline commit vs burst pricing?
04:12 Sofia: Absolutely. baseline: reserved capacity commit gives a discounted rate per token + reduced queuing. burst capacity billed at a higher per-token rate. For this uplift I'm proposing a 12-month amendment — 40% added reserved pool — that gives you roughly 18% blended discount across token compute. I'll send a revised quote.
04:45 Priya: Is there a minimum commit required for APAC enablement?
04:50 Sofia: Not strictly, but APAC reserve tiers start at a moderate size; we can do burst-only initially but recommend a small reserved pool to avoid cold penalties.
05:10 Lena: Regarding keys — can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS? we need customer-managed keys and HSM-backed protection for certain models.
05:22 Miles: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM in Private deployments. for hosted dedicated we can do bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) with restrictions. I'll put together a short KMS integration plan and a checklist.
06:05 Damien: The EU private option — is that the same as Redwood Private? what's the difference between dedicated and private again?
06:15 Sofia: Good question. Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our managed environment (shared control plane) with data isolation by tenancy. Redwood Private is customer-hosted control plane — VPC peering, customer-managed network, and can be deployed in your cloud project or on-prem; it gives you the strongest compliance posture but adds setup time.
07:00 Priya: For EU residency we need the Private stack. are there examples of customers who've done EU private ramp recently?
07:10 Miles: Yes, we've onboarded two retail customers this quarter and have a playbook. lead time typically 3–6 weeks for cloud-private in eu-west, on-prem is longer. we'll share the playbook.
07:35 Damien: About fallbacks — if the private region loses capacity, will requests route to hosted? we need to control fallback to avoid data egress.
07:50 Miles: By policy. we can configure routing policies to never fall back outside EU for certain routes. that'll be part of the rollout config.
08:30 Priya: Benchmarks — we'd like Redwood to run a benchmark with our traffic shape and a 10k request spike to see latency and token cost.
08:38 Miles: That's doable. we'll need your sample prompts, expected concurrency, and sequence-length distribution. then we can run a side-by-side compare (eu private vs dedicated eu-west vs apac burst).
09:10 Sofia: timeline — you mentioned Q4 peak. what's the internal preferred go-live?
09:17 Priya: We need APAC by Nov 15 and EU private by Oct 1 for regulatory sign-off. can that be achieved?
09:25 Miles: Oct 1 for EU cloud-private is tight but possible if Atlas provides compliance artifacts and we prioritize provisioning. APAC Nov 15 is achievable. both depend on legal and infra slots.
09:55 Damien: Contract terms — if we sign a 12-month extension with the +40% commit, can we include a mid-term re-evaluation clause? e.g., look at usage at month 6 and adjust?
10:08 Sofia: Yes, we can add a quarterly review clause and an adjustment mechanism. commercial teams typically do a mid-term uplift at agreed thresholds. I'll include language in the amendment.
10:35 Priya: On the security checklist — we need the pen test report, SOC2 type II, and encryption key rotation policy.
10:45 Lena: also need proof of RBAC for console and token-level auditability.
10:50 Miles: We'll attach the SOC2 pack and a redacted pen test summary. RBAC and token-level logs are supported; availability depends on deployment mode but in Private you'll get full audit capability.
11:30 Damien: Competitors — we've been piloting CloudModels Inc for a month; the latency was OK but costs were high. InHouseServing has good on-prem support but lacks the dev experience. curious how Redwood's rollout and support cadence compares.
11:50 Sofia: We focus on predictable SLOs and a dev-first console; plus our optimize toolkit gives actionable batching/quantization recommendations to reduce unit cost. support SLA depends on contract tier; we'll propose a Premium SLA for Atlas with 24/7 escalation during ramp.
12:40 Priya: Ok, that sounds promising. can you confirm expected delta in unit cost if we move from burst to reserved for their workload?
12:49 Miles: Ballpark, switching 40% of peak traffic to reserved should save ~15–25% on compute token costs depending on model mix and quantization. we'll provide a model-specific estimate in the quote.
13:30 Sofia: Next steps recap — I'll send the updated quote and contract amendment; Miles will run the benchmarks; Lena and I will connect on KMS; Atlas to share traffic and compliance docs.
13:45 Priya: we'll aim to send traffic histogram and compliance list by Monday.
13:55 Damien: schedule the benchmark and lock dates once quote is in.
14:05 Lena: thanks all. will look for the SOC2 pack.
14:12 Sofia: Great. any other open questions?
14:20 Priya: not from me.
14:24 Damien: none here.
14:30 Sofia: OK, we'll follow up — thanks everyone.
14:33 End of recording.

Notes about transcription quality: speaker overlap caused occasional mislabels; some product names (KY cache) were transcribed as KV-cache inconsistently, and apac vs asia region codes were sometimes inconsistent.
